To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MSeA enhances the apoptotic potency of chemotherapeutic drugs through interactions with JNK-dependent targets.
methyl selenium enhances apoptosis induced by selected chemotherapeutic agents in prostate cancer cells by a JNK-dependent mechanism.
methylseleninic (MSeA), an organic form of selenium, enhances apoptosis induced by chemotherapeutic drugs through a JNK-dependent mechanism in androgen-independent prostate cancer (PCA).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic agents for the treatment of human cancers and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which selenium exerts its anticancer activities.
the role of selenium and the mechanisms by which selenium may affect the development and progression of cancer.
the use of methylseleninic and selenite in the treatment of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the methylselenium derivative MSeA, but not the inorganic selenide Se2, enhances the apoptotic potency of the chemotherapeutic drugs SN38 (7-ethyl- 10-hydroxymethylcamptothecin), etoposide (VP16), and paclitaxol/taxol, in androgen-independent human prostate cancer cells.
methylseleninic acids (MSA) enhances apoptosis induced by cancer chemotherapeutic drugs, such as etoposide (VP16), SN38 and paclitaxol in prostate cancer (PCa) cells.

the methylselenol (MSe-) precursor MSeA enhanced the apoptosis potency of chemotherapeutic drugs, including topoisomerase inhibitors and paclitaxol/taxol, in DU145 and PC-3 human androgen-independent PCA cell lines through JNK-dependent and -independent pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of selenium with cancer therapeutic drugs can be used to enhance the apoptosis potency of these drugs and thus improve the chemotherapy of PCA.
the combination of MSeA and chemotherapeutic drugs may provide a novel approach for the treatment of androgen-independent prostate cancer.
the selenium compounds, methyl selenium, and selenite, have a synergistic effect on the apoptosis potency of cancer therapeutic drugs.

the combination of MSeA with SN38, etopo-side, or paclita- xel significantly increased apoptosis in PCA cells.
methylseleninic-acid (MSeA)-induced apoptosis is enhanced by topoisomerase inhibitors (SN38, etopside) or paclitaxe/taxol.
